messages:
Sam Chen: FYI we have a paying customer reporting repeated tokenized outputs after an SSE reconnect. They say sometimes the resumed stream repeats the last 1-2 tokens and in other cases emits a full duplicate completion.
Maria Lopez: Ugh. Do we have a repro? any request/response IDs from the customer?
Customer Support: They pasted a snippet with trace_id=tr_2026_03_01_9143, and said the client does a reconnect within ~300ms of a dropped socket. They included SDK v0.8.2 client logs.
Sam Chen: Can you paste the log? even a short excerpt helps.
Customer Support: "client: disconnected, attempting reconnect (attempt=1), resume_token=abc123.., pending_buffer=0
client: connected, sent resume token
server: accepted resume token, resume_offset=512
server: sse_chunk: [TOKENS: ...]"
Josh Patel: Quick theory: the client is re-sending any buffered input after reconnect AND the resume token is stale (doesn't include generation_id). If the server accepts and applies both the replay and the resumed stream we can get duplicated tail output.
Maria Lopez: That matches. The SDK's old resume token only encoded offset and session_id. Not generation or request nonce. If the client has aggressive retry and also flushes a local pending chunk, double-gen possible.
Sam Chen: Repro idea: run a short loop that opens an SSE, sends prompts with a small chunk, forcibly drop socket, then reconnect quickly. Use a captured resume_token vs a new-start. We should verify billing behavior too (do they get charged twice?).
Josh Patel: Can reproduce locally in ~1/20 runs with a tight reconnect (~200-400ms). I used the cURL SSE proxy and a toy client. Example repro (node):
```js
// pseudo-code
const sse = new SSEClient(url);
sse.send({prompt: 'a'});
setTimeout(()=>socket.destroy(), 50); // simulate network hiccup
setTimeout(()=>sse.reconnect({resume_token: savedToken}), 300);
// client auto-requeues any pending user message before reconnect
```
This shows both: client-side queued send + resume path applied.
Customer Support: Customer complaining about being billed for both outputs. They provided two invoice line items for same session time.
Maria Lopez: On billing: If two distinct completions were emitted by the server, it's expected they are billable. But if we can prove the second output was an accidental replay we might refund. We need root cause.
Sam Chen: Action items: 1) Get customer to upgrade to SDK v0.9.0-beta which includes resume tokens with generation_id and nonce. 2) Ask them to enable client-side dedupe flag (temporary) that prevents re-sending pending prompt on reconnect when a resume token is used. 3) Engineering: add server-side defensive check to ignore a re-applied input where resume_offset indicates those tokens were already produced.
Josh Patel: I dug into server logs for trace_id=tr_2026_03_01_9143: found two completions with same request_id prefix but different generation_ids (gen_47 vs gen_48). The resume acceptance path stamped gen_48 but the buffered resend arrived and created gen_47 first because of race. That explains ordering differences and duplicate content.
Maria Lopez: So not a pure duplicate of identical generation_id, but two separate gens created from race. We need to clarify semantics: resume should not accept replays at an earlier sequence window.
Sam Chen: Short-term mitigation: implement idempotency via client-supplied request_nonce that server records per session. If a resend has same nonce, drop it. Also add a server heuristic: if resume_offset <= last_emitted_offset then drop re-applied input.
Customer Support: Customer asked for repro steps we can share so they can validate their fix. Can we give them the minimal script?
Josh Patel: I'll paste a short shell repro they can run:
```bash
# start a minimal client (uses node script repro.js)
node repro.js --prompt-file small.txt --reconnect-delay 300 --force-disconnect 50
# repro.js will output the two completions when raced
```
I'll put repro code in tickets.
Maria Lopez: For billing/request follow-up: I propose we offer a one-time credit while we fix server guards. Escalate to Billing for manual refund of duplicate line once eng confirms duplicate-generation root cause.
Sam Chen: I'll create an internal bug with labels: sse, resume-token, idempotency, billing-impact. Assign to Josh. Also include the trace and logs.
eng-bot: Bug created: INF-5172 (sse/resume-token-race). Assignee: Josh Patel. Priority: P1.
Customer Support: Customer replied: "Thanks — we'll try the beta SDK and confirm by Monday. Appreciate the quick response." :thumbsup:
Maria Lopez: Thanks team. Josh, ping when you have a patch or need a shorttime rollback plan.
Josh Patel: Will do. Plan: server-side fallback in ~48h (config flag) then SDK rollout.
Sam Chen: Closing loop here — keep CS updated.
Customer Support: Marking as awaiting_customer.
